question: Fill in the blank: 'Neither the principal nor the teachers ___ present at the meeting.' 🏫
explanation: Spot on! When two subjects are connected by 'neither/nor', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. Here, 'teachers' is plural, so we use 'were'. ✨
hint: Look at the noun right next to the blank to decide if you need a singular or plural verb.

question: Choose the correct verb: 'Either the players or the coach ___ responsible for the strategy.' ⚽
explanation: Awesome! In an 'either/or' sentence, the verb matches the subject closest to it. Since 'coach' is singular, we use 'is'. 🎯
hint: Focus on the word 'coach' rather than 'players'.

question: Complete the sentence: 'The captain, as well as the players, ___ excited for the tournament.' 🏏
explanation: Brilliant! When subjects are joined by 'as well as', the verb always agrees with the first subject. 'The captain' is singular, so the verb is 'is'. 🌟
hint: Ignore the phrase stuck between the commas when picking your verb.

question: Fill in the blank: 'The students, along with their teacher, ___ going on a field trip.' 🚌
explanation: Perfect! With 'along with', the verb agrees with the main (first) subject. 'Students' is plural, so we use 'are'. 🎓
hint: Look at the very first noun in the sentence.

question: Choose the right verb: 'Bread and butter ___ my favorite breakfast.' 🍞
explanation: Great! Even though there's an 'and', 'bread and butter' represents a single idea or meal. So, it takes a singular verb. 🥞
hint: Think of the two items as a single dish.

question: Complete the sentence: 'Everyone in the class ___ finished the assignment.' 📝
explanation: Excellent! Indefinite pronouns like 'everyone', 'everybody', 'someone', and 'nobody' always take a singular verb. 💡
hint: Treat 'everyone' as a single collective group acting as one.

question: Fill in the blank: 'A number of students ___ participating in the science fair.' 🔬
explanation: Superb! The phrase 'a number of' always means 'many', so it takes a plural verb. 🚀
hint: Remember: 'A number of' = plural, 'The number of' = singular.

question: Choose the correct verb: 'The number of tickets available ___ very small.' 🎟️
explanation: Fantastic! The phrase 'the number of' refers to a specific single quantity, so it takes a singular verb. 📉
hint: You are talking about a specific single figure or count.

question: Complete the sentence: 'Fifty miles ___ a long distance to drive every day.' 🚗
explanation: Spot on! Expressions of time, money, weight, and distance take a singular verb when thought of as a single unit. 📍
hint: Think of 'fifty miles' as one single block of distance.

question: Fill in the blank: 'The news ___ broadcasted at 9 PM every night.' 📺
explanation: Awesome! Even though 'news' ends with an 's', it is considered an uncountable singular noun. 🗞️
hint: We don't say 'one new, two news'. It's always a singular concept.

question: Choose the right verb: 'The police ___ investigating the robbery.' 🚓
explanation: Brilliant! The noun 'police' is traditionally treated as a plural noun in English, so it takes a plural verb. 🚔
hint: Think of 'police' as a group of officers.

question: Complete the sentence: 'These scissors ___ very sharp.' ✂️
explanation: Perfect! Tools and clothes with two parts (scissors, trousers, glasses) take plural verbs unless preceded by 'a pair of'. 🧵
hint: It has two blades, so treat it as plural.

question: Fill in the blank: 'A pair of scissors ___ left on the table.' ✂️
explanation: Great! When we use 'a pair of', the subject is 'pair', which is singular. Thus, the verb is singular! 🖇️
hint: Focus on the word 'pair', not 'scissors'.

question: Choose the correct verb: 'Mathematics ___ my favorite subject.' 📐
explanation: Excellent! Academic subjects like Mathematics, Physics, and Economics end in 's' but are singular. 📚
hint: It's the name of one single subject.

question: Complete the sentence: 'The committee ___ agreed on the new policy.' 🏢
explanation: Superb! A collective noun like 'committee' takes a singular verb when the group acts together as a single unit. 👥
hint: They are acting as one unified group.

question: Fill in the blank: 'The committee ___ divided on their opinions.' 🏢
explanation: Fantastic! When members of a collective noun act individually or disagree, we use a plural verb. 💬
hint: They are showing different opinions, acting as individuals.

question: Choose the right verb: 'Not only the students but also the teacher ___ excited.' 🎉
explanation: Awesome! With 'not only... but also', the verb agrees with the noun closest to it. Here, 'teacher' is singular. 🎓
hint: Look at the word right before the blank.

question: Complete the sentence: 'Not only the manager but also the employees ___ attending the workshop.' 💼
explanation: Spot on! The verb must agree with the closest noun. Since 'employees' is plural, the verb is 'are'. 👥
hint: Which noun is closer to the verb?

question: Fill in the blank: 'The manager and owner of the store ___ here today.' 🏪
explanation: Brilliant! When two nouns are joined by 'and' but only the first has the article 'the', they refer to the same person. So, the verb is singular. 👤
hint: Notice there is only one 'the'. It's one person with two titles.

question: Choose the correct verb: 'The manager and the owner of the store ___ arriving soon.' 🏬
explanation: Perfect! Because 'the' is used before both nouns, they are two separate people. Therefore, a plural verb is needed. 👥
hint: Count the 'the's! There are two distinct people here.

question: Complete the sentence: 'One of the students ___ forgotten the homework.' 🎒
explanation: Great! The actual subject is 'One', not 'students'. Since 'One' is singular, the verb must be 'has'. 🎓
hint: Focus on the first word of the sentence.

question: Fill in the blank: 'Neither of the answers ___ correct.' ❌
explanation: Excellent! 'Neither of' means 'not one or the other', so it always takes a singular verb. 💡
hint: Think of it as 'Not a single one'.

question: Choose the right verb: 'Each of the boys ___ given a medal.' 🏅
explanation: Superb! 'Each of' emphasizes the individual, so it always takes a singular verb. 🥇
hint: Look at 'Each' rather than 'boys'.

question: Complete the sentence: 'The quality of the mangoes ___ excellent this year.' 🥭
explanation: Fantastic! The subject is 'quality', not 'mangoes'. 'Quality' is singular, so we use 'is'. ✨
hint: What is actually excellent? The mangoes themselves, or their quality?

question: Fill in the blank: 'Much of the effort ___ been wasted.' 🕰️
explanation: Awesome! 'Much' is an uncountable pronoun, so it takes a singular verb. ⚡
hint: You can't count 'effort' with numbers.

question: Choose the correct verb: 'Many students ___ going to the concert.' 🎸
explanation: Spot on! 'Many' refers to a plural countable noun, so it naturally takes a plural verb. 🎟️
hint: Students can be counted, and there are lots of them!

question: Complete the sentence: 'Some of the pie ___ eaten.' 🥧
explanation: Brilliant! With 'some of', look at the noun. 'Pie' is singular/uncountable here, so the verb is singular. 🍰
hint: Is 'pie' singular or plural in this sentence?

question: Fill in the blank: 'Some of the apples ___ rotten.' 🍎
explanation: Perfect! Here, 'some of' refers to 'apples', which is a countable plural noun. So, we use 'are'. 🧺
hint: Look at the word after 'some of'.

question: Choose the right verb: 'Nobody ___ the trouble I have seen.' 👀
explanation: Great! 'Nobody' is an indefinite pronoun and always acts as a singular subject. 🕵️‍♂️
hint: Treat words ending in -body or -one as singular.

question: Complete the sentence: 'Both of my friends ___ coming to the party.' 🎈
explanation: Excellent! The pronoun 'both' always implies two, meaning it is plural and takes a plural verb. 👯‍♀️
hint: 'Both' means two people.

question: Fill in the blank: 'A lot of water ___ spilled on the floor.' 💧
explanation: Superb! 'Water' is uncountable. When 'a lot of' is followed by an uncountable noun, the verb is singular. 🧽
hint: Can you count water? If not, use singular.

question: Choose the correct verb: 'A lot of coins ___ found in the treasure chest.' 🪙
explanation: Fantastic! 'Coins' are countable and plural. When 'a lot of' is followed by a plural noun, the verb is plural. 👑
hint: Look at the noun after 'a lot of'.

question: Complete the sentence: 'The rich ___ expected to help the poor.' 🏰
explanation: Awesome! When 'the' is followed by an adjective to refer to a whole class of people, it takes a plural verb. 🌍
hint: This means 'rich people', representing a group.

question: Fill in the blank: 'The jury ___ reached a unanimous verdict.' ⚖️
explanation: Spot on! Since the verdict is 'unanimous' (everyone agreed), the jury is acting as one single unit. 🔨
hint: They are agreeing and acting together as one.

question: Choose the right verb: 'The jury ___ arguing loudly among themselves.' ⚖️
explanation: Brilliant! Because the members are arguing, they are acting as individuals. Thus, a plural verb is used. 💬
hint: They are disagreeing, so they are not acting as one unit.

question: Complete the sentence: 'The Arabian Nights ___ a fascinating book.' 📖
explanation: Perfect! Even though the title ends in 's', it is the name of ONE single book, so it takes a singular verb. 📚
hint: It is the title of a single object.

question: Fill in the blank: 'Everything ___ going according to plan.' 📅
explanation: Great! Indefinite pronouns like 'everything', 'anything', and 'nothing' always take a singular verb. ⚙️
hint: Words ending in '-thing' are singular.

question: Choose the correct verb: 'Few ___ willing to volunteer for the tough task.' 🧗‍♂️
explanation: Excellent! The pronoun 'few' refers to a plural, countable number of people or things, so it takes a plural verb. 🧗‍♀️
hint: 'Few' always means more than one.

question: Complete the sentence: 'My family ___ going on a vacation next week.' ✈️
explanation: Superb! 'Family' is a collective noun acting as a single unit going on vacation together, taking a singular verb. 📸
hint: The group is doing the action together as one.

question: Fill in the blank: 'Two hours ___ a long time to wait for a train.' 🚆
explanation: Fantastic! Periods of time are treated as a single block or unit, requiring a singular verb. 🚉
hint: Think of 'two hours' as one period of time.

question: Choose the right verb: 'None of the cake ___ left for me.' 🎂
explanation: Awesome! 'Cake' is an uncountable noun here, so 'None' takes a singular verb. 🍽️
hint: Look at the word 'cake'. Can you count it in pieces here?

question: Complete the sentence: 'None of the players ___ tired.' 🏀
explanation: Spot on! When 'none of' is followed by a plural noun like 'players', it generally takes a plural verb in modern English. 🏃‍♀️
hint: Look at the plural noun 'players'.

question: Fill in the blank: 'Economics ___ completely changed my view of the world.' 🌍
explanation: Brilliant! Like Mathematics, Economics is a field of study. It ends in 's' but is singular. 📚
hint: It's one subject area.

question: Choose the correct verb: 'The staff ___ meeting in the conference room right now.' 👔
explanation: Perfect! 'Staff' acts as a singular collective unit here, so it takes a singular verb. (Note: in UK English, 'are' is also common, but NCERT generally accepts 'is' for collective groups acting as one). 💼
hint: They are acting together as a single group.

question: Complete the sentence: 'Every boy and girl ___ supposed to wear the school uniform.' 👕
explanation: Great! When two singular nouns joined by 'and' are preceded by 'each' or 'every', the verb must be singular. ✨
hint: The word 'Every' makes the whole subject singular.

question: Fill in the blank: 'A pen or a pencil ___ required for the exam.' ✏️
explanation: Excellent! When two singular subjects are connected by 'or', the verb is singular. 🖋️
hint: It's one OR the other, not both.

question: Choose the right verb: 'Apples or oranges ___ fine for the snack.' 🍎
explanation: Superb! When plural subjects are connected by 'or', the verb is plural. 🧺
hint: Both options given are plural.

question: Complete the sentence: 'More than one person ___ complained about the noise.' 🙉
explanation: Fantastic! Despite the meaning being plural, the grammatical phrase 'More than one' is followed by a singular noun and singular verb. 🗣️
hint: Look at the word 'person' right before the blank.

question: Fill in the blank: 'Half of the cake ___ eaten by the kids.' 🍰
explanation: Awesome! 'Cake' is a singular fraction subject here, so we use a singular verb. 🎂
hint: The cake is one whole item.

question: Choose the correct verb: 'Half of the students ___ passed the difficult exam.' 🎓
explanation: Spot on! 'Students' is a countable plural noun. When finding a fraction (half) of a plural group, the verb is plural. ✨
hint: Students are countable and plural.
